subject: Post-call: throughput SLOs, token economics & tier selection — action plan
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Blake <simon@wavehealth.ai>, Lena Park <lena@wavehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:10:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: throughput SLOs, token economics & tier selection — action plan

Hi Simon / Lena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a concrete set of next steps so we keep momentum with the integration and procurement teams. Major points we agreed on:

- Target feature: real-time clinical summarization for patient messages (95th pct SLO = 400 ms token streaming for 1–2 concurrent clinician sessions).
- Expected traffic (per your estimates): 120k monthly active users (MAUs) generating ~15M token-generation requests/month (~60M tokens/month). See attached MAU estimate.
- Budget guidance you gave: $8k–$18k/month target initially (preferred cap $15k/month) while we validate latency and quality.

Primary decision areas we discussed: tier selection (dedicated vs hosted), streaming vs batched response, and batching window sizing (latency vs $/1M token trade-off).

What I put together below are two pragmatic configuration options with estimated unit economics so you can evaluate against your $/month target. These are high-level — we can run a short POC with sample traffic to firm the numbers.

Option A — Hosted (standard) + streaming (low latency, higher unit cost)
- SLO: streaming 95th = 400 ms for 1–2 clinician sessions.
- Behavior: per-token streaming, minimal batching (batch window ~10 ms to preserve stream feel).
- Estimated effective cost: $1,200 per 1M tokens (includes streaming premium + prefix KV cache savings).
- For 60M tokens/month => ~$72k/month (exceeds your target).
- Upside: simplest integration, fastest time to value.

Option B — Dedicated reserved tier + mixed streaming + micro-batching (SLO-driven routing)
- SLO: route high-priority interactive sessions to dedicated instances (streaming, tight latency); route background summarization and lower-priority jobs to batch-optimized workers.
- Batching: background jobs batched to 50–100 ms windows, reducing per-token cost.
- Effective blended cost: ~ $220–$320 per 1M tokens depending on batch ratio and quantization profile.
- For 60M tokens/month => $13.2k–$19.2k/month (within / near your stated band).
- Upside: hits budget targets with policy-driven routing; requires reserved capacity commitment for dedicated pools.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm the 60M tokens/month ballpark (or provide revised MAU -> tokens CSV)? I attached our copy of your numbers.
2) Which SLO tier is non-negotiable? (A) 95th = 400 ms streaming for all sessions; (B) 95th = 400 ms only for "active clinician" sessions (2 per org) and relaxed for background.
3) If you prefer Option B, I can run a short cost simulation with different split ratios (e.g., 10% interactive / 90% batch vs 30%/70%) and return a 2-week POC plan.

I'll schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the simulation unless you'd rather I send it over first.

Attachments: wave_health_mau_estimates.csv, redwood_quickquote-v2.pdf

Cheers,

Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
Note: pricing estimates above are preliminary and assume model variant A-3 (quantized) with standard KV caching. We will provide precise numbers after traffic sampled POC.

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. Quick clarifications from our side: 

- The 60M tokens/month is our middle-case; the team provided a conservative and aggressive scenario in the attached CSV (conservative = 35M, aggressive = 95M).
- The procurement team is pushing for a cap nearer to $15k/month for the first 3 months.
- For the SLO: we need 95th = 400 ms for active clinician sessions (we can limit the count to initially 5 concurrent active sessions). Background summarization can be relaxed to 1–2s.

What we'd like to see from you next: a blended cost projection for the conservative/mid/aggressive token scenarios with (A) hosted streaming baseline and (B) dedicated mixed routing with a 10% interactive / 90% batch split. Also outline the minimum reservation commitment (GPU hours/month or monthly spend) to hit Option B pricing.

Simon

Simon —

Great, thanks for confirming the scenarios. Per your request I ran a quick blended projection and reservation sensitivity. Numbers below assume: model variant = A-3 quantized, KV cache hit rate = 35%, and dedicated pool uses a mix of A100-equivalent GPUs with runtime batching kernels.

Blended cost table (per 1M tokens):
- Hosted streaming: $1,200 / 1M tokens
- Dedicated mixed (10% interactive / 90% batch): $260 / 1M tokens (range $220–$320 depending on batch windows and quantization profile)

Monthly projections:
- Conservative (35M tokens): Hosted = $42k; Dedicated mixed = ~$9.1k (35*$260)
- Mid (60M tokens): Hosted = $72k; Dedicated mixed = ~$15.6k
- Aggressive (95M tokens): Hosted = $114k; Dedicated mixed = ~$24.7k

Reservation guidance for Option B:
- Minimum reservation to hit $260 / 1M band: reserve 2x A100-equivalent nodes (~1 full reserved pool) or commit to a $10k/month reserved spend for first 3 months. Lower commitments push unit cost higher due to spot/burst premiums.

Risk/operational notes:
- If interactive sessions spike above the reserved concurrency (5 concurrent), we can route overflow to hosted-tier at a slightly higher per-token cost. We can set automatic fallback policies to avoid dropped requests.
- We recommend a 2-week POC with representative request traces so we can validate the 35% cache hit assumption — that number materially affects the per-token math.

Proposed immediate plan:
1) I will assemble a short PDF with the three scenario tables + reservation sensitivity (deliverable: by EOD Monday).
2) Marissa will send a one-page SOW + procurement checklist for the reserved capacity path so procurement can review.
3) If Wave signs the $10k/month 3-month reservation, we'll kick off the POC within 5 business days.

Do you want the PDF first or the SOW?

Best,

Hannah
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
